goal.text: Clear the three judged findings blocking the gate-provisioning branch

tasks.task:
## What
The gate-provisioning change on this branch passes every deterministic check — the
publication gate reports `check: all deterministic checks passed (line coverage
100.00%)`. It fails the judged tier on three rules, all in the code it adds:

```
FAIL boundary_inputs_validated
  scripts/python-install.sh:40: UV_NO_SYNC is consumed by presence alone, so values
  such as "0" or "false" silently disable synchronization instead of being parsed or
  rejected.
FAIL changed_behavior_has_e2e
  scripts/python-install.sh:54-55: No end-to-end test verifies the new python-install
  preserved log's creation, permissions, or secret redaction.
FAIL comments_earn_their_place
  scripts/python-install.sh:2-19: The file header is an extended duplicate of the later
    UV_NO_SYNC, missing-lockfile, and --locked comments rather than a terse file-level
    purpose.
  tests/e2e/test_workspace_contract_e2e.py:1032-1043, 1067-1075, 1105-1118: docstrings
    repeat the historical narrative, the adjacent setup, and implementation detail at
    excessive length.
```

Clear all three.

**Take the first one seriously — it is a real defect, not a style note.** `UV_NO_SYNC=0`
and `UV_NO_SYNC=false` currently *disable* provisioning, which is the opposite of what
either spelling means to a reader. Decide the contract and make the code say it: either
parse the value and honour falsey spellings, or reject a value you will not honour. Do
not leave a switch whose "off" setting turns the thing off.

The second is a genuine coverage gap in this change's own new behaviour: it writes a
preserved log, and this repository's preserved logs are owner-only and secret-redacted
by contract. Cover that the way `scripts/preserved-log.sh`'s other callers are covered.

The third is prose. Cut the header to a terse file-level purpose and let the later
comments carry the specifics they already carry; cut the three docstrings to what the
setup and assertions do not already say.

## Why
This branch is what lets any engine adoption be verified at all — `just gate` currently
cannot check a change that moves a Python pin, and a four-pin adoption is blocked behind
it. It is worth landing correctly rather than quickly.

The `UV_NO_SYNC` finding matters beyond the rule. That variable is the escape hatch the
journeys use to keep pointing uv at an environment they already control; an escape hatch
that fires on `UV_NO_SYNC=0` will eventually be set that way by someone who means the
opposite, and provisioning will silently not happen. That is the same class of failure
this whole branch exists to fix: a step that quietly does not run, and a check that then
reads whatever was lying around.

## Acceptance criteria
- `UV_NO_SYNC` has a stated contract and the code implements it. Say which you chose and
  why, and cover the falsey spellings with a test.
- The preserved log's creation, permissions, and redaction are covered by an e2e journey.
  State how you drove it.
- The four prose sites are cut to what the code and assertions do not already say.
- `just lint-llm-diff origin/main` reports no findings. Report the run id.
- `just gate` is green. Report it.
- No `ignore` directive is added and `llmlint.yml` is not edited.
- Do not move any version pin, and change nothing else on the branch. The provisioning
  commit is finished work.
- Another manager's run is working in this repository concurrently in its own worktree;
  keep documentation edits to what this change requires.


## Working conditions on this host — read before your first edit
Another manager's run is executing concurrently here and one of its nodes reclaims
publication workspaces. It has already removed a live dispatch worktree out from under a
previous attempt at this exact task, mid-`just check`, losing that attempt's uncommitted
edits. This is not hypothetical and it is not something you can prevent.

Two consequences, both binding:

1. **Commit each fix the moment it works, before starting the next one.** Three findings,
   at least three commits. Do not batch them and commit at the end. A commit is in the
   branch and survives; a working tree does not.
2. **If your worktree disappears mid-turn** — `pwd` fails, your session path is gone, git
   stops resolving — do not investigate it, do not search clones, remotes, or publication
   checkouts for your commit, and do not try to recover the directory. It was deleted by
   a process outside this run. Report what you had completed and stop. A previous attempt
   spent its remaining turns hunting for a directory that no longer existed.

Your branch `onevcs/s-ccff01a9527e` already carries the provisioning change as
`d1872df0`. That commit is safe regardless of what happens to any worktree.
tasks.title: fix(gate): give UV_NO_SYNC a real contract and cover the preserved log
